strings.name: Jhumpa Lahiri
strings.summary: Raised in a Bengali family, Lahiri wrote in English about immigrant households, everyday estrangement and belonging. Interpreter of Maladies won the Pulitzer Prize; The Namesake and The Lowland expanded her fiction. After moving to Rome, she began writing in Italian and translating her own and others' work, making language learning and translation central creative concerns.

strings.influence.rationale: Portrays immigrant families and belonging in works such as Interpreter of Maladies, exploring literary identity and translation across languages.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in London; raised in Rhode Island, United States.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: English BA at Barnard; master's degrees including English and creative writing, and a Renaissance-studies PhD at Boston University.
strings.highlights.h1.title: The detail of immigrant families
strings.highlights.h1.text: Stories and novels examine Bengali families' relationships, loss and belonging.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Writing in Italian
strings.highlights.h2.text: Uses self-translation, Italian fiction and essays to rethink literary language.
strings.timeline.t1.title: St. Louis Literary Award
strings.timeline.t1.text: Accepted the annual university honor at the Sheldon Concert Hall.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Roman Stories in English
strings.timeline.t2.text: Her Italian stories were translated by Lahiri together with Todd Portnowitz.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Returned to Barnard
strings.timeline.t3.text: Became an English professor and director of creative writing at her alma mater.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Published an Italian novel
strings.timeline.t4.text: Dove mi trovo centers on an urban solitary figure; she later translated it as Whereabouts.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Published In altre parole
strings.timeline.t5.text: Reflected in Italian on language learning and her change of writing language.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Published The Lowland
strings.timeline.t6.text: A story of brothers, politics and migration reached the Booker and National Book Award shortlists.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Published The Namesake
strings.timeline.t7.text: Her first novel explored immigrant identity through names and generations.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First story collection
strings.timeline.t8.text: Interpreter of Maladies won the Pulitzer Prize the next year, establishing her career.
